summary: Spun out of the 2026-08-08 H3 speed report. Evidence gathered live: the engine's own process cmdline carries --lowvram, the app log says 'Set vram state to: LOW_VRAM', and the bench bat carries no flag. Deliberately opened as an INVESTIGATION, not a fix - the cause is unproven and --lowvram exists for a measured reason.

Hypothesis DISPROVEN before spending a generation. Read the shipped model_management.py: LOW_VRAM and NORMAL_VRAM share one branch and one budget, and no other vram_state branch tells them apart, so the flag is inert under aimdo exactly as docs/builder/02-image-and-rebuild.md already said. The proposed isolation test would have measured nothing - cancelled. Card reframed onto the half-wire that survives: the Pod dropped the flag on measurement and the local engine never followed. Two user corrections recorded, both of which the earlier draft had wrong: we DID ship GGUF and it OOM'd (MPI-168/185/190), and offload works with or without the flag.

Better suspect than the vram flag, found off a user question about how the offload split is sized. ComfyUI DOES size it from conditioning - estimate_memory asks each model for extra_conds_shapes and memory_required sums them with the noise shape - but class MiniMaxH3 declares neither memory_usage_factor_conds nor an extra_conds_shapes override, while Flux2, Qwen and the whole Wan family do. So H3's budget is computed from the output latent alone and the references count as zero. Recorded as a source-verified FACT with the causal link to the slowdown flagged as unmeasured inference. Points at --reserve-vram as the lever and an upstream PR as the real fix.
